# Chain length and privileged-action density in the AI Village dataset

*Generated by `analysis/ai_village_chains.py`. Source: `aidigestorg/ai-village` (AI Digest), research terms; aggregate statistics only. Privileged classes are assigned by regex over bash commands and tool arguments, mirroring Charter §5: P1 out-of-workspace file operations, P2 network, P3 credentials, P4 spawning another agent. The classifier is syntactic and content-blind; it is an under-count (GUI actions that reach the network through a browser are not visible to it).*

## B. Claude Code agent (Opus 4.5 on the Claude Agent SDK, 2026-01-26 to 2026-04-02)

### Per computer-session span: world tool calls n, privileged-class calls k (polling, chat and memory calls excluded)

- sessions: 1,006
- chain length n: mean 16.8; median 8; p90 44; p99 100
- privileged-class actions k: mean 3.45; median 2; p90 9; p99 30
- privileged share of actions k/n: 0.205
- sessions with **no** privileged action (a declaration gate costs them nothing): 38.0%
- sessions with 3 or more: 39.1%

| per-action survival p | uniform tax: mean pⁿ | declaration gate: mean pᵏ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.862 | 0.968 |
| 0.95 | 0.588 | 0.868 |
| 0.9 | 0.438 | 0.779 |

Tool calls made outside any computer-session span: 12,708 world actions, 8,272 privileged (65.1%); these are the agent working from its SDK loop directly and are not chained here.

Tool mix (all sessions): mcp__village__computer_use 7,124, Read 4,686, mcp__village__bash 4,363, Bash 540, Edit 79, Grep 45, Write 24, mcp__village__request_google_sign_in 21, Glob 10, WebSearch 8, WebFetch 3

Privileged classes (session-level counts): P1 679, P2 3,226, P3 193

**Subagent spawns (P4):** none. This agent never used the SDK's Task tool in two months, so the laundering surface measured in RESULTS.md §4 does not occur in this stream.

## A. Computer-use sessions, all agents (2025-04-02 to 2026-09-19)

### Per session: actions n, privileged-class bash actions k

- sessions: 78,111
- chain length n: mean 31.1; median 40; p90 41; p99 44
- privileged-class actions k: mean 5.99; median 1; p90 20; p99 36
- privileged share of actions k/n: 0.192
- sessions with **no** privileged action (a declaration gate costs them nothing): 42.5%
- sessions with 3 or more: 44.3%

| per-action survival p | uniform tax: mean pⁿ | declaration gate: mean pᵏ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.738 | 0.945 |
| 0.95 | 0.267 | 0.796 |
| 0.9 | 0.120 | 0.695 |

Bash actions are 40.3% of all actions; GUI actions (click, type, scroll) are the rest and are not classified, so k is a floor.

| model family | sessions | mean n | mean k | share k=0 | k/n |

Privileged classes (session-level counts): P1 210,584, P2 334,099, P3 55,320, P4 13,160

## Reading

1. **Chain length in the Village is set by the scaffold, not the task.** The computer-use median is
   exactly 40 actions with p90 at 41: after 2026-03-24 agents consolidate memory every ~40 actions
   and start a new session (CHANGELOG). The Claude Code agent, which ran its own loop, has a median
   of 8 and a long tail to 100. Any argument that friction works by decaying long chains inherits
   whatever the scaffold decided the chain length should be. This is a second reason, beside
   RESULTS.md §3, not to build the containment story on chain length.
2. **Privileged-class density is the quantity that transfers.** About one action in five is in a
   privileged class in both streams (k/n 0.19 and 0.21), with a floor from unclassified GUI actions.
   The share is stable across model families except the "other" group (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Grok,
   Muse), where it doubles; Gemini agents reach the network through bash least.
3. **What a declaration gate would have cost here.** 42% of computer-use sessions and 38% of
   Claude Code chains contain no privileged action and would pay nothing. At a per-privileged-action
   survival of 0.95, mean session survival under the declaration gate is 0.80 (computer use) and 0.87
   (Claude Code), against 0.27 and 0.59 under a uniform per-step tax at the same p. The gap is the
   throughput case for keying friction to a syntactic class rather than to every step, and it is
   consistent with the Suite A cost measured in the harness (0.74 → 0.72, 0.84 → 0.76).
4. **Spawning is rare but present.** 13,160 session-level P4 matches in computer use (bash patterns
   that launch another agent or a detached process) against zero Task-tool spawns by the Claude
   Code agent. The Charter §6 question, whether the constraints travel with the spawn, cannot be
   answered from bash text; it needs the instruction, which the harness logs and this dataset does not.

*Caveats. The classifier is regex over command text and tool arguments: it under-counts network access
through GUI browsers, over-counts P1 on any absolute path outside a handful of home roots, and treats
`[REDACTED]` credential strings as P3 only when the surrounding command names a credential. Numbers are
per-session aggregates; no session content is reproduced. Dataset: AI Digest, AI Village, research terms.*
